structure: One ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-11-16.md, 19 lines in three pieces: a title line ("Ruling: Sam, 16 November 2026"); a one-line preamble saying it was given in the overview-and-review build session, answering the status page's question on plants' customs document code; and a numbered list of two decisions. Decision 1 (3 lines) is the plants customs document code, C085 (CHED-PP) against C640 staying the animals code (CHED-A), and carries the only verbatim words of Sam in the file — "sounds like you've got a good shout on what the plants should be, just do the plants code" — plus the note that it unblocks req-2002 and inc-199. Decision 2 (11 lines) is the longer one: no new "Submitted action required" status, a notification submitted with outstanding items is SUBMITTED, agreed with Syed Islam on 16 November; it withdraws the 9 October afternoon ruling's "Submitted action required" status (req-902's status, req-1987's new status) and the 'Action required' tag on the live-animals list (inc-131's action-required criteria); it has a "What stays" clause (the submitted date and the outstanding items left at that moment, req-909); it names what comes out with the status (the status tag reads 'Submitted'; the view's action-required warning, its 'Continue' and the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error — req-902, req-903, req-907) until the banner design is agreed; it carries one sentence explicitly marked "Orchestrator's call, applying the ruling narrowly" (nothing action-required is shown until that design lands); and it closes that "Completed" stays out until a real source of completion exists, none does today. The scope is the whole file, so nothing is left out. The file names no page file, view, component or repo path, gives no wording for the future banner and no design for it, and decides nothing about any status other than SUBMITTED and the withdrawn "Submitted action required" and "Completed". Note for the reader, not for a claim: sources.json records that decision 2's "What stays" clause is later replaced by ruling:sam-2026-11-19, which keeps only the submitted date; this extract claims the file as written and precedence is the reconciler's.

parts.title: The whole ruling: plants customs document code C085, and no "Submitted action required" status
parts.scope: The entire file, every line of it: the title, the preamble, decision 1 with Sam's verbatim quote, and the whole of decision 2 including its withdrawal clause, its "What stays" clause, what comes out with the status, the sentence marked as the orchestrator's call, and the closing "Completed" line. Nothing in this source belongs to another part.
covers: Decision 1: plants' customs document code is C085, the CDS document code for the Common Health Entry Document for Plants, Plant Products and Other Objects (CHED-PP) — one claim, verbatim against Sam's quoted words "sounds like you've got a good shout on what the plants should be, just do the plants code" where they support it, inferred where the specific code and its expansion go beyond the quote, with the statement saying what in the quote implies it.
Decision 1's second half: C640 stays the animals code (CHED-A) — claimed, as its own claim or recorded with the C085 claim.
Decision 1's effect: it unblocks req-2002 and inc-199 — named in the claim's note, since it says which earlier blocked requirement and row the ruling releases.

Decision 2's core: no new "Submitted action required" status is introduced; a notification submitted with outstanding items, such as a missing health certificate, is SUBMITTED like any other. The file quotes no speech of Sam here, so quote is the file's own words of the decision, and the claim says so.

Decision 2's ground: agreed with Syed Islam on 16 November, that a status which does not align with the notification flow is not introduced, and that outstanding actions are shown through a banner-style alert which the dashboard designs under test introduce.

Decision 2's withdrawal clause, each withdrawn item named: the 9 October afternoon ruling's "Submitted action required" status (req-902's status and req-1987's new status), and the 'Action required' tag on the live-animals list (inc-131's action-required criteria).

Decision 2's "What stays" clause: submitting records its date and the outstanding items left at that moment (req-909), since a future banner needs them — claimed as the file writes it, with its req reference in ref or note.

Decision 2's list of what comes out with the status until the banner design is agreed: the notification's status tag reads 'Submitted'; the view's action-required warning comes out; its 'Continue' comes out; the review's 'Upload a valid health certificate' error comes out (req-902, req-903, req-907).

The sentence the file marks "Orchestrator's call, applying the ruling narrowly: nothing action-required is shown until that design lands" — recorded as the orchestrator's application of Sam's ruling, not as a ruling of Sam's, said so in the claim's statement or note.
The closing line: "Completed" stays out until a real source of completion exists, and none does today.

What the ruling leaves open, each as a gap claim with an empty quote: the banner-style alert's own design, wording and placement (the dashboard designs under test are said to introduce it, but the file specifies nothing about it); when and how anything action-required may be shown once that design lands; and what a real source of completion would be, needed before "Completed" returns.

The preamble's framing fact: the ruling was given in the overview-and-review build session, answering the status page's question on plants' customs document code — recorded where it bears on a claim's scope, and otherwise used as the note's context.

A question is not a decision: nothing in the file that only floats or asks is recorded as a decision — only decisions 1 and 2 and the marked orchestrator's call are, and the rest of the file's statements are claimed as what the ruling relies on or leaves open.

ref on every claim naming the file and the list item, such as "ruling-sam-2026-11-16.md claim 1" or "ruling-sam-2026-11-16.md claim 2"; note on each saying which report question and conflict it answers, or that it is new.
